overall: All 40 source URLs resolved and every licence and may_publish claim matched the Commons or Met record; no answer made a wrong 'yes, may publish', and both flagged CC BY-SA ShareAlike where relevant. Differences were in fit and credit quality: the side that pasted auto-generated credits (scraped titles such as 'Dutch: Zingende engelen', Wikidata label strings, or a collection named as creator) lost licence points wherever it appeared. Picks often coincided (Hammershoi, Hobbema, Whistler, Turner), so briefs were decided by the second image; literal on-brief photographs (seeded loaf, choir row, river confluences, beam lighthouse) generally beat famous paintings chosen as loose metaphors. A few descriptions overstated what is in the picture (Hammershoi 'empty' left half, the ESO dish 'under a dark star field'), and one answer admitted describing an image it had not seen.
